description: Source-backed contract for the reusable FOnline AngelScript GUI object model, screen stack, layout, rendering, input dispatch, project hooks, and validation boundaries.

scope.support_note: The CoreScripts GUI runtime is production-used but remains experimental until it has a standalone client example, focused runtime fixtures, and an explicit compatibility policy.
included: Gui.fos object types, documented members, callbacks, enums, setting, events, and top-level screen API
screen registration, creation, stacking, focus, modal, cursor, drag-and-drop, and lifecycle behavior
anchor, dock, crop, 9-slice, text, grid, item-view, and scroll behavior implemented by the reusable runtime
Input.fos mouse and keyboard state, dispatch, repeat, and input-loss behavior
the project hooks required to drive the runtime from client lifecycle and render events
excluded: .fogui, .foguischeme, XML, JSON, or any other declarative GUI authoring format
project-owned GUI generators, visual editors, generated screen catalogs, layouts, styles, and widget libraries
project screen identifiers beyond the Engine-owned GuiScreen::None sentinel
project font bindings, image catalogs, localization policy, input actions, gameplay presentation, and accessibility acceptance
Dear ImGui developer tooling, server host windows, native application chrome, and touch-to-GUI adaptation

type_notes.Object: Base tree node for activity, geometry, hierarchy, hit testing, focus, dragging, callbacks, lookup, and recursive drawing.
type_notes.Panel: Object with a sprite background, optional 9-slice frame, crop/scissor, and animated vertical or horizontal scrolling.
type_notes.Text: Drawable text node using a bound FontType, FontFlag set, colors, skip-lines state, and optional height measurement.
type_notes.TextInput: Focused editable text node with length, password, carriage, clipboard, and on-screen-keyboard behavior.
type_notes.Button: Panel with pressed, hover, disabled, switched, and condition state.
type_notes.CheckBox: Button with checked state and an OnCheckedChanged callback.
type_notes.RadioButton: CheckBox that clears switched sibling radio buttons under the same parent.
type_notes.Screen: Top-level panel with registration id, modal/multiinstance/close-on-miss behavior, cursor set, movement policy, and top-of-stack state.
type_notes.Grid: Panel that clones a named prototype node into indexed cells and lays them out by columns and padding.
type_notes.MessageBox: Text-derived timestamped message feed with type filtering, inversion, scrolling, and a project-configurable default inversion setting.
type_notes.Console: TextInput-derived command console with activation, history persistence, and submit behavior.
type_notes.ItemView: Grid that obtains client Item handles, filters or sorts them, binds live handles to cells, and invokes item drawing callbacks.

screen_api_notes.RegisterScreen: Replace any existing registration for an id, store its factory, and precache one instance; multiinstance screens discard that temporary instance.
screen_api_notes.ShowScreen: Show the existing single-instance screen or create a new multiinstance screen, move it to the top, and run show/appear callbacks.
screen_api_notes.HideScreen: Hide one active screen selected by top-of-stack, id, or direct handle.
screen_api_notes.HideAllScreens: Hide active screens from the top until no active screen remains.
screen_api_notes.BringToFront: Move an active screen to the top and transition appear/disappear state without recreating it.
screen_api_notes.GetScreen: Return the registered single instance or the last multiinstance screen for an id.
screen_api_notes.GetActiveScreen: Return the top active screen, optionally restricted to one id.
screen_api_notes.IsScreenActive: Report whether an active screen exists for an id.
screen_api_notes.GetActiveScreens: Return active screens in current stack order.
screen_api_notes.GetFocusedObjects: Drop inactive focused nodes and return a clone of the current focus set.
screen_api_notes.SetFocusedObject: Clear prior focus and focus one node or its complete FocusGroup subtree.
screen_api_notes.AddFocusRecursively: Add an object subtree to the current focus set.
screen_api_notes.GetPressedObject: Return the current pressed node after clearing inactive state.
screen_api_notes.GetLastPressedObject: Return the most recent pressed node after clearing inactive state.
screen_api_notes.GetDraggedObject: Return the current pressed node only when it has entered dragging state.
screen_api_notes.GetHoveredObject: Return the current hovered node after clearing inactive state.
screen_api_notes.NextTextInput: Advance focus to the next active TextInput in the active screen tree.
screen_api_notes.CollectMessageBoxes: Collect MessageBox nodes from all screens or one object subtree.
screen_api_notes.IsConsoleActive: Report whether any active Console exists globally or under one subtree.
screen_api_notes.AddDragAndDropHandler: Append a handler evaluated in registration order after a dragged mouse release.
screen_api_notes.SetDropMenu: Install the optional external drop-menu input and drawing adapter.
screen_api_notes.CheckHit: Report whether any active screen tree contains a hittable node at a position.
screen_api_notes.IsModalScreenActive: Report whether any active screen is modal.

annotation_notes.GuiScreen: Engine declares only None; embedding projects extend the enum with their screen ids.
annotation_notes.CursorType: Engine declares only Default; embedding projects may extend cursor modes.
annotation_notes.AnchorStyle: Bit flags selecting parent edges; an unselected axis is centered against the authored parent base size.
annotation_notes.DockStyle: Exclusive edge/fill layout modes that take precedence over anchor positioning.
annotation_notes.Gui.MsgboxInvert: Client setting used as the MessageBox default inversion policy.
annotation_notes.Game.OnScreenChange: Fires after a successful show or hide with the screen id and parameter dictionary.
annotation_notes.Game.OnConsoleMessage: Fires when the reusable Console submits a message.

lifecycle_rules.name: Project screen initializer
lifecycle_rules.requirement: Provide namespace GuiScreens with void InitializeScreens(); EngineCallback_Start calls it and cannot compile or start without that project contract.
lifecycle_rules.rationale: The reusable runtime owns screen mechanics but intentionally does not own a game screen catalog.

lifecycle_rules.name: Registration and precache
lifecycle_rules.requirement: Register each non-None GuiScreen id with a factory; registration replaces the old entry and constructs one screen immediately for initialization and resource precache.
lifecycle_rules.rationale: Registration is executable client startup work, not passive metadata loading.

lifecycle_rules.name: Single and multiinstance ownership
lifecycle_rules.requirement: Reuse a registered single-instance screen; create a fresh screen for each multiinstance show and remove that instance after hide.
lifecycle_rules.rationale: The flag changes construction, persistence, lookup, and teardown semantics.

lifecycle_rules.name: Show and hide callback order
lifecycle_rules.requirement: Treat Show as active-state setup, OnShow traversal, then OnAppear traversal; treat Hide as OnDisappear, OnHide traversal, inactive state, event fire, and optional multiinstance removal.
lifecycle_rules.rationale: Project callbacks often distinguish data refresh from top-of-stack visibility.

lifecycle_rules.name: Cursor screen ownership
lifecycle_rules.requirement: Register GuiScreen::Cursor as the dedicated always-active CursorScreen and draw it explicitly through EngineCallback_DrawCursor.
lifecycle_rules.rationale: The cursor is excluded from the ordinary screen stack and ordinary screen draw pass.

lifecycle_rules.name: Explicit resolution and language refresh
lifecycle_rules.requirement: Call Callback_OnResolutionChanged after viewport changes and Callback_OnLanguageChanged after language changes.
lifecycle_rules.rationale: The reusable runtime does not subscribe these project lifecycle transitions itself.

layout_rules.name: Parent coordinate space
layout_rules.requirement: Interpret authored positions and sizes relative to the parent; root objects use Settings.View.ScreenWidth and ScreenHeight as the live parent size.
layout_rules.rationale: The same layout algorithm serves nested widgets and viewport-level screens.

layout_rules.name: Dock precedence
layout_rules.requirement: When Dock is not None, use the selected Left, Right, Top, Bottom, or Fill rule and ignore Anchor positioning.
layout_rules.rationale: Dock and Anchor are alternative layout modes rather than cumulative constraints.

layout_rules.name: Anchor and centering
layout_rules.requirement: Anchor selected axes to parent edges; center an axis with no matching edge bit by half the live-size minus authored-base-size delta.
layout_rules.rationale: Unanchored controls remain centered when a parent or viewport changes size.

layout_rules.name: Crop affects drawing and hit testing
layout_rules.requirement: When Panel crop is enabled, scissor descendant drawing and reject hit tests outside the panel rectangle.
layout_rules.rationale: Visual clipping and interaction clipping must agree.

layout_rules.name: 9-slice frame
layout_rules.requirement: Use SetFrameImage plus nonnegative cap insets measured in source pixels; the runtime clamps source and destination caps and stretches edges and center.
layout_rules.rationale: Frame images can resize without distorting corners or producing invalid UV ranges.

layout_rules.name: Panel scrolling
layout_rules.requirement: Enable vertical and/or horizontal auto-scroll explicitly; target changes animate for PanelScrollAnimationDurationMs and drawing refreshes active tweens.
layout_rules.rationale: Scroll values are stateful layout offsets rather than a renderer-only transform.

layout_rules.name: Grid prototype cloning
layout_rules.requirement: Point Grid at a named object prototype, choose a positive column count, and let ResizeGrid clone, index, initialize, and position the cells.
layout_rules.rationale: The prototype remains hidden while clones become the live repeated content.

input_rules.name: Input event subscriptions
input_rules.requirement: Include Input.fos once; its ModuleInit subscribes mouse, key, and input-loss Game events and forwards them to Gui engine callbacks.
input_rules.rationale: Projects should not duplicate the same forwarding subscriptions.

input_rules.name: Active-screen hit order
input_rules.requirement: Mouse input starts at the top active screen; children are tested from last to first so later children are visually and interactively above earlier siblings.
input_rules.rationale: Screen stack and tree order jointly define hit priority.

input_rules.name: Modal and close-on-miss behavior
input_rules.requirement: Close a close-on-miss screen on an unhandled left click; only a nonmodal screen may search lower active screens for a hit and bring one forward.
input_rules.rationale: Modal screens block fallthrough while nonmodal windows can be reordered by interaction.

input_rules.name: Keyboard dispatch order
input_rules.requirement: Dispatch global input to active screens from top to bottom, then the active console, then focused objects when the console is absent or inactive.
input_rules.rationale: Global shortcuts, command entry, and focused controls have distinct precedence.

input_rules.name: Pressed-object repeat
input_rules.requirement: After mouse down, begin repeated pressed callbacks after 500 ms and continue every 40 ms while the pointer still hits the pressed object.
input_rules.rationale: Controls that use OnMousePressed depend on these fixed timings.

input_rules.name: Drag and drop
input_rules.requirement: Start dragging from a draggable pressed object, draw it in the cursor pass, and evaluate registered drop handlers in order until one returns true.
input_rules.rationale: The runtime owns gesture and dispatch mechanics while projects own transfer semantics.

input_rules.name: Input-loss reset
input_rules.requirement: On focus/input loss, release tracked keys and mouse buttons, unhover and unfocus objects, cancel a pressed object as lost, and notify the drop menu.
input_rules.rationale: Alt-tab and window-focus changes must not leave sticky input or drag state.

integration_rules.name: No Engine declarative GUI format
integration_rules.requirement: Treat Gui.fos and Input.fos as an AngelScript runtime API; do not claim that Engine parses .fogui, .foguischeme, or another layout format.
integration_rules.rationale: Declarative sources and generators belong to embedding projects or a separately versioned companion tool.

anchors: project-owned metadata or generated GUI contracts

integration_rules.name: Client hook bridge
integration_rules.requirement: Call EngineCallback_Start, EngineCallback_Loop, EngineCallback_Draw, and optionally EngineCallback_DrawCursor from the embedding client's corresponding events.
integration_rules.rationale: The runtime implements these hooks but does not subscribe project render/lifecycle events for itself.

integration_rules.name: Script render scope
integration_rules.requirement: Draw GUI only from the client OnRenderIface scope where script drawing is enabled; place the cursor pass at the project-selected top layer.
integration_rules.rationale: Native ClientEngine enables script drawing around OnRenderIface and processes video before ending the scene.

integration_rules.name: Font and image dependencies
integration_rules.requirement: Bind every FontType used by Text nodes and deliver every sprite referenced by Panel or Button before showing affected screens.
integration_rules.rationale: The GUI runtime delegates text layout and sprite loading/drawing to the reusable font and image systems.

integration_rules.name: Project enum extension
integration_rules.requirement: Extend GuiScreen and CursorType through project metadata without redefining the Engine sentinels.
integration_rules.rationale: Engine supplies reusable baseline values while each game owns its screen and cursor catalog.

integration_rules.name: Touch adaptation boundary
integration_rules.requirement: Do not assume Input.fos routes native touch events into GUI mouse callbacks; provide and validate project/platform adaptation when touch interaction is required.
integration_rules.rationale: ClientEngine emits separate touch events while the reusable Input module subscribes only mouse, key, and input-loss events.

validation_rules.name: Generated runtime contract
validation_rules.requirement: Regenerate and check gui-runtime.json and its reference pages whenever Gui.fos, Input.fos, client input/render dispatch, or this interface manifest changes.
validation_rules.rationale: The model fails on class/API/callback/annotation/timing/source drift before prose can silently become stale.

validation_rules.name: Embedding client compilation
validation_rules.requirement: Compile and bake an embedding client that supplies project enum values, GuiScreens::InitializeScreens, screen factories, and lifecycle/render hook calls.
validation_rules.rationale: Engine-only source checks cannot prove the required cross-module AngelScript symbols or generated screen code.

validation_rules.name: Visible layout and input
validation_rules.requirement: Validate representative screens at every supported resolution and input profile, including anchors, docks, crop, 9-slice, focus, close-on-miss, modal ordering, repeat, drag, and input loss.
validation_rules.rationale: Compilation and headless execution do not prove geometry, draw order, alpha hit testing, clipping, or user interaction.

validation_rules.name: Language and font acceptance
validation_rules.requirement: Switch every shipped language in a visible client, run Callback_OnLanguageChanged, and inspect wrapping, clipping, glyph coverage, focus colors, text input, and message feeds.
validation_rules.rationale: The GUI runtime refreshes text callbacks and geometry but cannot validate project translations or bound font coverage.

validation_rules.name: Focused fixture gap
validation_rules.requirement: Keep the surface experimental until Engine has a self-contained client fixture that constructs screens, drives input, renders pixels, changes resolution/language, and proves teardown.
validation_rules.rationale: Current native tests do not directly execute the CoreScripts GUI runtime.
